mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by > 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rose by > 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by > 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the last month, combined with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreased > 100k and UNRATE rose > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last three months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increased over the last 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) is stagnant or declining, it indicates a supply-side slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects weaken.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% for 2 quarters and INDPRO stagnant/declining
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 1% for 2 quarters and INDPRO is stagnant/declining.
